Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-prompt-long-0150", "row_sha256": "963fed0258c3e4b1e6b8b51057af5ccb0949087246da948a7005b8e040834755", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
hey, can you turn these notes into a dinner calendar for our household for march 9 through march 22, inclusive? just dinners, not lunches or breakfasts, and please show the date and weekday for each one. it’s for Maya, Leon, Iris, who is ten, and Theo, who is six. My mum Jo comes for dinner on the two dates below, so those meals are for five. everyone else is four. we usually try to eat at 6:30, but on a couple of days that won’t work, so keep the timing notes with the date instead of making them all look the same.

some food things first because they matter for the whole calendar: Maya doesn’t eat red meat, but fish is fine. Leon has a peanut allergy, so no peanuts in the meal or in a suggested sauce or topping. Iris doesn’t eat mushrooms; if mushrooms are included at all, they would need to be kept separate, but probably easier not to plan around them. Theo can’t have ordinary milk or cream. oat milk is okay for him and hard cheese is okay too. don’t treat any of those as preferences that can be ignored on one night. we do have a separate toaster and cutting board for allergy-safe prep, but don’t need a long safety explanation in the calendar.

we already have a few things written in the shared calendar, so please keep those as they are rather than replacing them with a different meal. monday march 9 is lentil soup, and there’s enough for four. tuesday march 10 Jo is coming at 6:30, and the calendar says salmon with rice; that is still the plan and should stay for five. thursday march 12 is dinner at Jo’s house, not a meal to cook here, but it should still appear as dinner at Jo’s for five. friday march 13 is takeaway; don’t pick the restaurant or say what food it is. saturday march 14 Maya is out until late and the note says use leftovers, so leave it as leftovers and don’t schedule a new cooked dinner. sunday march 15 we have a family cooking slot at 4:00, though nobody has chosen what to make yet. keep that time and the fact that it is undecided, don’t fill in a dish for that date just to make the calendar look complete.

for the rest of the open nights, make suggestions using what we have, but it doesn’t have to use every ingredient. pantry has brown rice, couscous, canned chickpeas, lentils, tomato paste, coconut milk, oats, and two cans of tuna. fridge has carrots, spinach, a half cabbage, lemons, oat milk, eggs, and hard cheese. freezer has peas, cod portions for four, and one container of vegetable stock. the spinach needs using by wednesday march 11, and the cabbage is best used by saturday march 14. eggs are fine throughout the whole two weeks. please don’t assume we have other fresh produce or meat. if a suggested meal needs an ingredient we don’t have, mark that it needs buying rather than pretending it is already here.

there are some schedule limits on the other dates. wednesday march 11 Iris has soccer and we get home around 6:15, so dinner should be ready quickly or be something we can prep ahead; keep it to about 25 minutes of active work. wednesday march 18 Leon works late and won’t be home until 7:15, so put dinner at 7:30 that night, not 6:30. tuesday march 17 is open, but we have a parent meeting from 5:30 to 6:15, so no long cooking session then. saturday march 21 we’ll be out from 2:00 and back around 6:00, so a meal that can be prepared before we leave would fit. all other open dinners can be around 6:30. don’t shift any fixed calendar item to solve a timing conflict.

could you make the result easy to scan, with one entry per date, and mark which entries are already fixed and which are suggestions? add a short prep or timing note only where it helps explain the schedule or a buying need, not a full recipe. if you mention ingredients, keep the allergy and food limits above in mind. use the food that needs using soon where it makes sense, but it’s okay if we don’t use everything. please don’t make up activities, guests, or calendar notes for any of the other days.

my current assessment is that there are enough pantry and freezer items to cover several open meals, but not enough information to say that every suggested dinner can be made without a shop. if a meal depends on an item outside the list, identify that need; don’t turn this assessment into a claim that shopping is definitely required for the whole two weeks. the calendar should cover only march 9 through march 22 and only dinner, and the march 15 cooking slot should remain undecided unless we get a separate choice from the family.", "output": "Create a dinner calendar for March 9 through March 22, inclusive. Include one entry per date, with the date and weekday, and cover dinner only—not breakfast or lunch. The household is Maya, Leon, Iris (10), and Theo (6). Jo joins for dinner on March 10 and March 12, so those meals are for five; other meals are for four. Dinner is usually around 6:30, subject to the timing notes below.

### Food requirements
- Maya does not eat red meat; fish is fine.
- Leon has a peanut allergy. Do not include peanuts in a meal, sauce, or topping.
- Iris does not eat mushrooms. If mushrooms are included, keep them separate; it may be easier not to plan around them.
- Theo cannot have ordinary milk or cream. Oat milk and hard cheese are okay.
- Treat these as requirements for every meal, not preferences that can be set aside. A separate toaster and cutting board are available for allergy-safe preparation; a long safety explanation is not needed.

### Fixed calendar entries
Keep these entries as written rather than replacing them with different meals:
1. **Monday, March 9:** Lentil soup; enough for four.
2. **Tuesday, March 10:** Jo is coming at 6:30. Salmon with rice is already planned and should remain on the calendar for five.
3. **Thursday, March 12:** Dinner at Jo’s house for five. This is not a meal to cook at home, but include it in the calendar.
4. **Friday, March 13:** Takeaway. Do not choose a restaurant or specify the food.
5. **Saturday, March 14:** Maya is out until late. The existing note says to use leftovers; do not schedule a newly cooked dinner.
6. **Sunday, March 15:** Family cooking slot at 4:00. What to make is undecided, so keep the time and undecided status without adding a dish.

### Available food
Use these items for suggestions where they make sense; it is not necessary to use everything. Do not assume other fresh produce or meat is available. If a suggested meal needs an ingredient not listed, mark it as something to buy rather than treating it as already available.
- **Pantry:** brown rice, couscous, canned chickpeas, lentils, tomato paste, coconut milk, oats, and two cans of tuna.
- **Fridge:** carrots, spinach, half a cabbage, lemons, oat milk, eggs, and hard cheese.
- **Freezer:** peas, cod portions for four, and one container of vegetable stock.
- Use the spinach by Wednesday, March 11, if practical. The cabbage is best used by Saturday, March 14. Eggs are fine throughout the two weeks.

### Timing and schedule notes
- **Wednesday, March 11:** Iris has soccer, and the family gets home around 6:15. Suggest a dinner that is ready quickly or can be prepared ahead, with about 25 minutes or less of active work.
- **Tuesday, March 17:** The date is open, but there is a parent meeting from 5:30 to 6:15. Avoid a long cooking session at that time.
- **Wednesday, March 18:** Leon works late and will be home at 7:15. Set dinner for 7:30, not 6:30.
- **Saturday, March 21:** The family will be out from 2:00 and back around 6:00. A meal that can be prepared before leaving would fit.
- Other open dinners can be around 6:30. Do not move a fixed calendar entry to resolve a timing conflict.

Make the calendar easy to scan and distinguish fixed entries from suggestions. Include a brief prep or timing note only when useful for the schedule or a buying need, not a full recipe. Keep all food restrictions in mind and do not invent activities, guests, or calendar notes for other days.

The current assessment is that the pantry and freezer contain enough to cover several open meals, but there is not enough information to say every suggested dinner can be made without shopping. Identify any listed-meal ingredient needs that fall outside the available-food list; do not claim that shopping is definitely required for the whole two weeks. Cover only March 9 through March 22 and dinner only. Leave the March 15 cooking slot undecided unless the family makes a separate choice."}]
